slice: Compare independently planned type-inference variants within one executable

decision.scope: First-execution controls calibrate, and this diagnostic does not reproduce the earlier roughly 0.5% increase. It does not establish equivalence of the original two release executables.
decision.replay_caveat: The same-before replay median retains a positive self-comparison interval of about +0.024% to +0.051%; do not credit small replay effects as a candidate speed change.
decision.next_step: Preserve this result separately from the release-binary observations. Any release-path acceptance must pass controls that retain separately compiled executables and independently generated native plans.

method.question: Does the type shortcut affect execution after independent planning, with native randomized tables and within-process controls?
method.switch: One executable; a temporary AtomicU8 selects original inference (0) or the five-line shortcut (1) before each independent plan. During execution value 2 panics if matching-float type inference is reached. No native hash implementation or seed change.
method.plans: Each pair is independently parsed, resolved, optimized and physically planned under its label mode. Distinct top-level Arc pointers and exact physical plan display are checked. Each plan retains its own native randomized IN filter. No plan or filter is cloned between labels.
method.orders: ABBA/BAAB execution order alternates within each process. Planning order alternates every two pairs, independently of execution order. All four combinations are balanced. order_flip rotates both directions across processes.
method.statistics: Per process: median independent-plan percentage change for first execution (primary) and mean of two executions (replay), plus full-label mean changes for both. Summaries are medians across processes; 10000 whole-process bootstrap samples stratified within four predetermined blocks, seed 88. No within-process independence claim.
method.controls: Same-before and same-after each have 16 processes. Primary first-execution median and full-label mean 95% intervals must fit +/-1%; inspect resolved bias. Also report replay controls. Paired has 32 processes.
method.candidate_interpretation: Only interpret sub-percent differences if controls calibrate. Report all four estimates. Upper intervals below +0.5% with no resolved positive effect are diagnostic evidence, not automatic production adoption. Keep original release observations separate.
method.stopping_rule: One fixed 64-process schedule, no extensions for a preferred answer, no discarded timings. Builds, source inspection and tests finish before measurement.
limits: Single-executable comparison removes between-binary layout effects; it does not establish equivalence of the original two release executables.
Retained plans and repeated execution differ from the original one-execution-per-plan protocol. First-execution statistics are kept separate.
Temporary switch overhead makes recorded planning times diagnostic, not a new planning speed estimate.
Aggregate perf counters contain both labels and must not be presented as per-label work differences.

source.identity: One executable, accepted add-zero runtime, unchanged native randomized IN hasher. Only the benchmark and a temporary type-inference switch differ from the frozen source. Dependency versions, features, profiles and lockfile match.
source.restoration: All shared sources, lockfiles and executable slots are restored and hash checked.

limitations: Single-executable comparison removes between-binary layout effects; it does not establish equivalence of the original two release executables.
Retained plans and repeated execution differ from the original one-execution-per-plan protocol. First-execution statistics are kept separate.
Temporary switch overhead makes recorded planning times diagnostic, not a new planning speed estimate.
Aggregate perf counters contain both labels and must not be presented as per-label work differences.
Each independently created plan is formatted and compared with its frozen physical-plan display before timing; those common verification allocations can change allocation history.
The execution trap covers matching FLOAT/DOUBLE type inference in this selected query. It is not a proof for all DataFusion workloads.
First-execution control intervals include zero, but the same-before replay median has a small resolved positive bias. Both are reported.
Conditional bootstrap intervals describe this host and fixed schedule without multiple-comparison correction.
The earlier release mean interval of [+0.045%, +1.819%] and later failed release self-comparison remain retained and unresolved by this diagnostic.

Run sequentially, finishing builds and verification before measurement. The build helper restores shared files in finally.
